title: Largest String After Removing K Characters
statement:
You are given a string `s` of lowercase English letters and an integer `K`. Remove **exactly** `K` characters from `s` (the remaining characters keep their original relative order) so that the resulting string is **lexicographically largest** among all possible results.

Print that string. Because `K < |s|`, the result is never empty. All candidate results have the same length `|s| - K`, so comparison is the ordinary dictionary order.

**Follow-up:** the interviewer expected a monotonic-stack solution; a dynamic-programming formulation over subproblems is possible but needlessly heavy.
inputFormat:
The first line contains the string `s`.
The second line contains the integer `K`.
outputFormat: Print the lexicographically largest string obtainable by removing exactly `K` characters.
constraints: s consists of lowercase English letters

examples.explanation: Three characters must remain. Remove the leading `b` so the string starts with `c`, then remove the `a` so that `b` follows. The result `cbc` beats every other 3-character subsequence such as `cab`, `bcc` or `abc`.
The string is already non-increasing, so removing the last character keeps the larger prefix `zy`.
Removing two of the three `a` characters leaves `ab`, which is larger than `aa`.

hints: Build the answer left to right. When a new character is larger than the last character you kept, keeping the old one is wasteful if you still may delete.
Use a stack: while you still have deletions left and the top of the stack is smaller than the incoming character, pop it. Then push the incoming character.
If deletions are left over at the end, the stack is non-increasing, so remove the excess from the end of the stack.
